Among Us surprised me. I didn’t know this game existed until one of my friends urged me to pick it up and I’m glad I did. Among Us is a hidden role deduction game where up to 10 players are preparing their ship. You can either be randomly be a crewmate or an imposter. Crewmates are given a list of tasks, which can either be quick or long, that they should do. While they’re traveling all around the map, keeping their eyes open is key as they can walk past a dead body, even walk in on the imposter doing imposter-only actions, and making sure that crisis are taken care of. If you find a dead body, you’ll get the option to report it and be sent to the discussion table so you can relay where you found it, who maybe was in the area or left, and hear what the others have to say in relation to alibis. You can also vote who you think the imposter is and if the majority agrees, they’ll get ejected. Though, you can hit the emergency meeting button if you have some juicy information. If you happen to be killed, or wrongly voted off, you can still do your tasks. Dead crewmates unfinished tasks still count in everyone’s combined completion bar. There are also areas where you can loosely monitor everyone with security cams, a heart monitor, or detectors that loosely detect how many people are in a room or the thresholds they passed.

Meanwhile, imposters (which can be between 1-3 depending on the host) need to blend in. They’re given a list of fake tasks so they can go to the station and pretend they’re doing it, but you won’t actually get the screen. Of course, you need to make sure that nobody notices that the shared completion bar isn’t moving when you’re “doing tasks”. If you believe you and a crewmate are alone, and hopefully no one is going to come right around the corner, you can kill them and widdle down the cremate’s numbers (assuming the cooldown is done). You can also sabotage the crewmates by locking doors and causing crisis that will kill the crewmates if they don’t deal with it or hamper them such as lowering their visibility. You can also jump into vents to quickly get out of an area and act like you totally weren’t there or hide and suddenly jump out when a poor lone sole walks along. Hopefully, no one walks in on you or keep everyone’s suspicions off you and on someone else.

For the crewmates to win, they either have to find and vote out all impostors or have everyone complete their tasks. While imposters can win by killing most of the crewmates (if the number of impostors equal cremates, the impostors win) or hope that the crewmates totally ignore the crisis.

For the low price of $5, Among Us is definitely worth it. There’s still a lot of people playing, which was one of my concerns, there’s a good variety of tasks, and it is pretty fun (albeit the frustrations that come with playing role games with strangers). Of course, with games like this, it’s best to play with friends if you can since you can use Discord to voice chat instead of the in-game text chat. [strike]Though, right now there is a language barrier between English players and Filipino players only wanting to speak Tagalog (and random vote people even with evidence pointing to the real imposter) on English servers. However, I have heard the developers have made a Tagalog server/filter that is currently in beta.[/strike] FIlipino servers have left beta and added into the main version!

[H1]Introduction[/H1]
At the time of this review, [I]Among Us[/I] needs little introduction. The hype around this game is real. It delivers the goods when it comes to fun, accessible gameplay. What better way to spend a few hours reconnecting with your friends, whom you’re socially/physically distanced from, than by either deducing who among you are the imposters/saboteurs, or by killing them or sabotaging their chances of survival?

[H1]What the Game Did Well[/H1]
The best thing about [I]Among Us[/I] is its simplicity. I have friends, who haven’t played this game before until recently, quickly pick up on the nuances of the gameplay after a couple of tries. The minigames you’ll need to complete for survival are varied, easy to figure out, and fun. [I]Among Us[/I] wasn’t designed to frustrate you with the details, but to simply provide you with enough distractions so that you’ll have a harder and more enjoyable time figuring out who the imposters/saboteurs are.

[I]Among Us[/I] can be played on your PC and on your mobile devices. It supports crossplay for Steam, itch.io, iOS and Android. This means practically everyone around the world can play together regardless of your preference in gaming platforms. Online games, including private matches, are simple to set up. Everything about [I]Among Us[/I] is about accessibility and quickly getting you to the fun part.

Depending on who you play with, [I]Among Us[/I] is really about the moments. It’s about you and your friends trying to figuring out who the culprits are, covering your tracks and lying to avoid getting caught, everybody ganging up on the suspects, feeling relieved when you rid of the correct imposter, feeling guilty when you didn’t, feeling relieved when you survived the menace, and feeling triumphant when you succeed as the imposter/saboteur. It’s these moments when you feel you’re connected to the people you’re playing with.

[H1]What the Game Could Have Done Better[/H1]
To keep the game size small, [I]Among Us[/I] lacks an in-game voice chat function. Built-in text chat is available, which is the safer option when playing with strangers. Yet when I play with close friends, I prefer to use voice chat so we can have livelier and more productive discussions. My friends and I use a third-party client to talk to each other while playing, which is just another thing we have to set up before getting to the fun bit.

[H1]What the Game Did Poorly[/H1]
You still need to purchase DLCs to access some cosmetics (e.g. pets, skins) for the Steam version, even though it is a paid version of the game. iOS and Android versions are free, though players of those versions will have to sit through ads in between matches.

[H1]Final Thoughts[/H1]
If you haven’t played [I]Among Us[/I] yet, do yourself a favour and get this game, whether it be on the PC or on your mobile devices. At some point, someone in your social circle will mention it, and you’ll be invited to play with them. This game truly delivers the goods when it comes to great fun. Despite its dark theme of murdering and sabotaging your crewmates (i.e. your friends), its presentation is whimsical and simple. Even casual players will find it captivating.

[b][i]Among Us[/i][/b] takes place in space, where players can have one of two roles: crewmate or imposter. The crewmates’ objective is to complete the assigned tasks and try to identify the imposter(s). The imposters’ objective is to sabotage and kill the crewmates without getting caught.

If a body is found, the crewmate or imposter can report the body, which then brings all players into a meeting to discuss who they think the imposter is. They then vote for who they think is the imposter.

While crewmates have to complete various tasks spread around the map and identify the imposters, the imposters have to sabotage the mission and kill the crewmates without being detected. Due to the simple yet potentially confusing nature of the game, winning matches can be incredibly hard, especially if you have only recently started playing [b][i]Among Us[/i][/b].

This game is a great way to have fun with friends or random people online and socialize. I would recommend this game to everyone.

Among Us is an online and local party game from 2018.
The game is about teamwork and betrayal for 4-10 players. There are currently 3 different maps. The players have to compete a few simple tasks and there is an imposter (or more - maximum 3) who has to kill the other crew members and prevent them from completing the tasks.
If someone finds a corpse and reports it or by pressing a buzzer a crew meeting takes place where people are sharing their opinion who could be the imposter and they have to vote who will be thrown out. The communication is done by typing, there is no voice chat ingame. For the most fun it is recommended (but not necessary) to use some voice chat program like Discord or Teamspeak.
The match ends if all tasks are done, the imposters have been voted out or not enough crew members are left to vote the imposter out.
Among Us is a simple game, there are no complex gaming mechanics but it is so much fun! It is a good example that it is not all about high end graphics.
Initially Among Us was mostly unnoticed by gamers, the game had barely players in its first year but after some streamers started to play it and maybe because of Corona the playerbase exploded and it reached an all time player peak of 438524. This unexpected boom made the developers to cancel their plans to make Among Us 2 and keep updating the current game.
Among us is also available on Android and IOS and features crossplay but no cross-progression.
It is free on mobile (with advertising) but you should invest the 3,99 € and maybe buy some skin DLC's (or buy some skins on mobile) just to support the developers.

Among Us, the game that took 2020 by storm and became a global phenomenon overnight really deserves the praise. While a simplistic game at first sight, it makes for a great party game, especially if you can get a large enough group of friends to play it.

The premise is pretty simple; you play as a crew member aboard a spaceship, and there are impostors among the crew (up to 3, depending on server settings and the number of players), who try to sabotage the ship and kill everyone inside. As a crewmate, you have tasks to complete; completing all tasks makes the crew win, though you can also try to figure out who the impostors are in order to eject them. As impostor, like I mentioned, you get to sabotage the ship, and your main goal is to kill everybody; you can also use vents to hide, and even during voting sessions, you can try to convince the crewmates that someone else is the impostor, and have them ejected.

While I mentioned a spaceship in the previous paragraph, there's two more maps in the game, each with their own design and tasks. While the gameplay between maps remains largely similar, it can still lead to variations in gameplay; for example, I feel the Polus map is better suited for full lobbies (10 people) rather than smaller groups. And beyond that, if you get a group on Discord, you can even invent custom gamemodes, like hide and seek!

I started playing this game by recommendation of my sister, and ever since then, I've played it pretty much every weekend with her and her group of friends. As I said, it's great fun, especially if you chat over Discord; accusing each other on voice chat is really fun!

Recently, given the huge boost in popularity it received, the devs actually decided to drop plans for a sequel, focusing instead on improving this game. And honestly, that's a great idea; they won't be dividing the playerbase, and there's lots of room for improvement. I really recommend this game!

[b]Among Us took the gaming world by storm, proving that sometimes, the simplest games create the most unforgettable moments. Whether you're completing tasks like a diligent crewmate or plotting deception as an imposter, this game is all about strategy, teamwork, and betrayal.

The gameplay is easy to understand but leads to intense, hilarious, and sometimes frustrating interactions. One moment, you're quietly fixing wires, and the next, you're passionately defending yourself in an emergency meeting after being falsely accused. The mix of deduction and deception makes every round unpredictable and fun.

What makes Among Us special is the social experience. It thrives on communication (and miscommunication), whether you're playing with friends or random players. The joy of convincing others to vote someone off, only to realize they were innocent, creates endless entertainment.

Visually, it's simple and colorful, with cute character designs that contrast the brutal reality of getting ejected into space. The sound design, from the satisfying task completion beeps to the ominous kill animations, adds to the tension.

While Among Us is at its best with a group of friends, public lobbies can be hit-or-miss, depending on how people play. The game has also evolved with new roles, maps, and customization options, keeping things fresh for long-time players.

In conclusion, Among Us is a fantastic party game that blends strategy and chaos in the best way possible. It’s proof that great multiplayer experiences don’t need complex mechanics—just a solid concept and the right group of people. If you love games that test friendships and create hilarious memories, this one’s a must-play![/b]

Gameplay:
You play as a Crewmate, or an Imposter, randomly chosen at the start of each round. To win as a Crewmate, 1 of 2 things must happen: 1. You and every other Crewmate must complete every task assigned to each of you, or 2. All Imposters must be voted off the group. To win as an Imposter, you must kill, frame, and/or otherwise reduce the total number of Crewmates until you cannot be eliminated. This happens when the number of live Crewmates is equal to or less than the number of live Imposters. Which leads nicely into...

Voting. Voting is how you live, and die. It is everything. The crew knows they have been infiltrated (they're told so at the beginning of every round, after all), so they have established a "Lost"-style elimination procedure: Whenever a corpse is found, Crewmates (or Imposters looking to avoid suspicion!) can report it, and an Emergency Meeting will be called to discuss what is to be done. As an Imposter, throw the crew off the trail; establish an alibi by the time the body is found, frame someone else for the murder, etc. (A little tip: if your fellow Imposter is definitely caught, don't be afraid to vote them off too. Among Us is one of the most engaging and memorable multiplayer games I have ever played. Despite its simple appearance, the game offers a surprisingly deep social experience that encourages teamwork, communication, critical thinking, and strategy.

One of the greatest strengths of Among Us is how it brings people together. Every match creates unique situations where players must work as a team to complete tasks while also trying to determine who can be trusted. The discussions and debates that take place during meetings are often intense, exciting, and genuinely entertaining.

The game's design is easy to understand, making it accessible to players of all skill levels. At the same time, mastering deception, observation, and deduction provides a rewarding challenge that keeps the gameplay fresh even after many hours.

The developers have also done an excellent job supporting the game with new maps, roles, customization options, and quality-of-life improvements. These updates have helped maintain the game's popularity and replay value over time.

Overall, Among Us is a fantastic example of how a simple concept can create an incredibly compelling experience. Its combination of strategy, social interaction, and suspense makes it a standout title that continues to be enjoyable years after its release. I highly recommend it to anyone looking for a fun and meaningful multiplayer game.
